description: Illustrative foreign official retreat from Treasury auctions over the CBO baseline horizon. Foreign auction shares are scaled by security type so that the removed participation equals the official share of foreign holdings in TIC SLT Table 3 for July 2026: official 354.4 of 1,464.9 billion dollars of bills and 3,418.7 of 7,783.2 billion dollars of notes, bonds and other coupon securities. The gradual retreat halves official participation; the official exit removes it. Released shares go to domestic nonbanks or to banks. Rate paths are imposed from a published long-run coefficient applied to the simulated foreign shortfall, not model outputs.
boundaries: Illustrative scenario accounting, not a forecast or causal estimate
Foreign holdings decline through reduced auction participation and maturity runoff; no secondary-market foreign sales are simulated
TDCSim represents foreign official and private holders as one Foreign sector with one maturity profile, settling through US banks
Each rate path is computed once from the matching quantity-only run and imposed on the scenario; it is not re-solved for the extra issuance that higher interest requires

Every scenario puts the TGA on the operating-cash path at each fiscal-year end (within a year it sits below the path by issuance awaiting settlement), so additional interest is financed by additional issuance from the start

calibration.holder_shift: Official share of foreign bills 0.2419; official share of foreign coupon securities 0.4392 (TIC SLT Table 3, July 2026). Gradual retreat multiplier = 1 - 0.5 x official share; exit multiplier = 1 - official share; rounded to three decimals
calibration.rate_rule: The 10-year shift at each quarterly curve date equals the coefficient times the foreign holdings shortfall from the family baseline as a percentage of marketable debt held by banks, the Federal Reserve, foreign and domestic nonbank holders at that date. Central 7 basis points per percentage point, the long-run coefficient of Bertaut, DeMarco, Kamin and Tryon (2012) for the foreign official share of Treasuries and agencies; high 14. Zero at two years and below, half at five years, full at ten years and beyond, log-tenor linear between
sources: Bertaut, DeMarco, Kamin and Tryon (2012), Journal of International Economics 88(2): 219-234; Federal Reserve IFDP 1028, p. 21
Treasury International Capital SLT Table 3, July 2026
